chapters.fx: What to watch: Fed's Collins spoke at 3pm CT — no verifiable readout yet at NY close, treat her remarks as unpriced. Then the weekend dead zone: the next real test is CPI Wednesday Oct 14, 7:30am CT — core m/m of 0.2% or below validates disinflation; 0.3%+ revives October (currently ~17.7%).
chapters.meaning: What changed: Friday's data pulled the Fed's two mandates in opposite directions — U Mich sentiment fell to 46.3 (vs 47.5 expected), a third straight monthly decline, with current conditions at a record-low 44.7. But the inflation-expectations lines the Fed actually watches both moved the wrong way: 1y expectations up to 4.7% (from 4.6%), 5y up to 3.5% (from 3.4%) — the second straight monthly rise, the highest since May. Thread: the hawkish-hold thesis is in its third week — FOMC minutes had 'most' officials seeing another hike by year-end, Waller/Musalem/Kashkari all spoke hawkish Thursday, December is ~83% priced, October ~17.7% (the pause), and claims held 197k for a fourth straight week near 57-year lows. What it means: this confirms and hardens the prior thesis. The Fed looks through sentiment; it does not look through expectations — 5y at 3.5% is exactly the unanchoring signal that keeps December alive. The dollar barely moved (DXY ~102.0, -0.1%), which is the market's way of saying Friday's data changed nothing about the rate path.

scenarios.base: Hawkish hold into the Oct 27–28 FOMC; USD stays bid while Dec odds hold near 80%+.
scenarios.bear: Soft CPI or a dovish FOMC surprise collapses hike odds; crowded USD longs unwind.
scenarios.bull: Oct 14 CPI beats expectations — Dec gets fully priced and DXY extends to fresh highs.

chapters.meaning: What changed: nothing material today — EUR/USD drifted to ~1.12 (−0.1% on the day, range 1.1188–1.1243), off Monday's 17-month low of 1.1161. The French selloff stabilized and the OAT–Bund spread sits ~140–146bp, off the >150bp wides. The pair is headed for a fifth straight weekly fall (−0.3% on the week, more than 3% over five weeks) — but the selling momentum is waning, as StoneX's Matt Simpson put it: you only get two or three big moves a year on the euro, and this was one of them. Thread: four weeks of French fiscal stress layered onto ECB-policy drag. Yesterday's edition said the relief-bounce hope broke; today's tape says the bleeding paused, not reversed. What it means: confirms the morning thesis — EUR/USD pinned near 1.12, the fiscal risk premium off the wides but not gone.

What it means: confirms — sterling remains the relative winner of Europe's fiscal stress, bid vs the euro and floored by BoE hike pricing.

chapters.fx: What to watch: Canada CPI Oct 21, then the BoC decision + MPR Oct 28. The ~161bp US–Canada 2Y gap is the anchor now — any CAD rally fights it until oil re-prices or the BoC talks hawkish again.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the story of the day — Canada lost 68,300 jobs in September against expectations of +9,200, the second straight monthly loss after −41,700 in August; 110,000 jobs gone in two months. Unemployment rose to 6.5%, participation fell to 64.8% — the lowest in 29 years outside the pandemic. USD/CAD jumped to ~1.4280, an 18-month low for the loonie and its fifth straight weekly loss. Oct 28 BoC hike odds collapsed to 25% from 40%; Canada's 2Y yield fell ~7bp to 3.183% — ~161bp below the US 2Y, the widest gap since February 2025. WTI softer near ~$91 added no help. Thread: this morning's edition (pre-print) had CAD as the oil-spike winner with the jobs report as the next test — the test failed. The losses were public-sector led (healthcare, education, −58,400) and youth employment fell ~48,000, so this is a domestic-demand story, not a tariffs story. What it means: this breaks the hawkish-BoC thesis outright. The market now prices the BoC on hold at best — a currency that was trading the oil premium is now trading the rate gap. Cross-check on the price action: the loonie fell on the miss and USD/CAD pushed to 18-month highs — the tape agrees with the numbers.

scenarios.bear: Canada CPI soft Oct 21 — BoC leans dovish, USD/CAD extends toward 1.45.
scenarios.bull: Hot Canada CPI + firm WTI — hawkish whispers return, CAD recovers some ground.

chapters.fx: What to watch: the spread itself — toward $5 means the geopolitical premium is truly unwinding; past $15 means Hormuz risk is back. For CAD, WTI is the number that moves the terms of trade; for JPY/EUR importers, Brent.
chapters.meaning: What changed: crude slipped further Friday — Brent down ~1% to ~$103.30, WTI ~$91 — as the no-strikes pledge held into the weekend. ING summed up the tape: the oil market is 'reluctant to price out the geopolitical premium' above $100 despite improved Gulf supply. Thread: the swing factor for CAD all week — every escalation headline lifted it, every de-escalation headline pressed it back down. What it means: the number that matters isn't either price, it's the ~$12.10 gap between them — roughly triple the normal spread. That wide gap is the geopolitical premium made visible: it lives in Brent, the seaborne benchmark exposed to Hormuz, while WTI, landlocked in Oklahoma, barely feels it. One wrinkle the morning edition flagged and today confirmed: with Canada's domestic story breaking (the −68.3K jobs miss), the loonie's oil tailwind now fights a widening rate gap — terms of trade giveth, policy taketh away. Japan and the eurozone, pricing imports off Brent, still get relief: cheaper energy eases import bills, a quiet positive for JPY and EUR.

scenarios.base: Brent drifts $100–105 into the weekend; CAD trades the BoC repricing more than the oil tape.
scenarios.bear: Ceasefire chatter or OPEC+ supply signals: Brent breaks under $100, spread collapses toward $5; CAD extends the jobs-driven slide, importers breathe easier.
scenarios.bull: A fresh escalation or Hormuz disruption: Brent spikes toward $110+, spread blows past $15; CAD rips on WTI follow-through, JPY/EUR sag on import-cost fears.

chapters.fx: What to watch: a break back above $4,300 would signal the haven bid is broadening beyond dollar-weakness — historically a USD-negative, CHF/JPY-positive setup. Conversely, a hot CPI Wednesday that revives hike bets would likely knock gold back toward $4,000.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold bounced toward ~$4,150 as the dollar softened and yields eased — still on track for a weekly loss. Thread: gold topped $5,318 in late January at the peak of the Iran escalation scare, then bled lower for months as the Fed's hawkish hold kept real yields elevated and the dollar ripped to 18-month highs. What it means: gold is trading as the anti-dollar right now, not the war hedge — it rises when the dollar softens and yields fall, which is exactly Friday's tape. For FX, firm gold is a soft headwind for USD and a quiet tell on risk appetite: when gold and soft-dollar move together, the market is hedging the dollar, not fearing the world.

scenarios.bear: Hot CPI revives the October hike; real yields jump and gold slides back toward $4,000.
